title: Real Estate Hoarding Design: What to Write, 12 Ideas and RERA Rules

faqs.question: What is a real estate hoarding?
faqs.answer: A real estate hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board that promotes a property project or broker. It can stand on a roadside, a junction unipole, a building wall or the project's own boundary. Its job is to make passers-by remember the project name and know how to enquire.

faqs.question: What should a real estate hoarding include?
faqs.answer: Five things: one headline of about seven words or fewer, one strong image, the project name and logo, one call to action such as a large WhatsApp number or short web address, and the RERA registration number with the authority's website, plus a QR code where the state requires one.

faqs.question: How many words should a hoarding have?
faqs.answer: As few as possible. Outdoor advertising guides commonly recommend seven words or fewer for the main message, because drivers see a board for only a few seconds. Faster roads need even fewer words, so test the design by reading it aloud in about three seconds.

faqs.question: Is the RERA number mandatory on a property hoarding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 11(2) of the RERA Act, 2016 says every advertisement by a promoter must prominently mention the RERA authority's website and include the project's registration number. A hoarding is an advertisement, so the number must be on it and readable from where people see it.

faqs.question: Is a QR code required on real estate hoardings?
faqs.answer: In some states, yes. UP RERA has required each project's QR code in advertisements since July 2024, and MahaRERA requires a scannable QR code on all ads, including hoardings, placed at the top right. Check your state authority's current directions before printing.

faqs.question: What are the common types of real estate hoarding?
faqs.answer: Roadside hoardings and billboards, unipoles at junctions, site hoardings on the boundary wall, directional boards that guide visitors to the site, wall branding in nearby localities, and panels at bus shelters, metro stations and malls where people wait and have time to read.

faqs.question: How do I know which hoarding brings leads?
faqs.answer: Give each board its own way to respond: a separate WhatsApp number or pre-filled message, or a tagged short link or QR code. Send people to a matching project page, then compare enquiries and site visits per board after a month and move budget to the locations that work.

faqs.question: Do hoardings need permission?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Outdoor advertising normally needs permission from the local body, such as the municipal corporation or development authority, under its advertising rules. Media owners who rent sites usually handle it, but check it is in place, including for hoardings on your own boundary wall.

faqs.question: What are the most common hoarding design mistakes?
faqs.answer: Too many words, an unreadable RERA number or missing QR code, several phone numbers, a render that does not match the site, no way to track enquiries per board, and old launch boards left up long after the offer has ended.
